title: KelpDAO/Kelp shows no grants or ecosystem-funding program on either domain — reconsider funder role
summary: Kelp's site now lives at kerneldao.com/kelp/ (kelpdao.xyz 301-redirects there, confirmed via curl and WebFetch). Fetching that page directly, the only funding-shaped mechanism found is a security bug bounty ('Secure Kelp, earn up to $250K') — not a grants or ecosystem-funding program. The org file currently tags roles:[funder] on the strength of an earlier pass; two independent fetches this round (old and new domain) found nothing that would qualify. Recommend the owner review whether KelpDAO should carry roles:[funder] at all, or be downgraded/removed pending evidence of an actual grants program.

title: polygon.technology/grow now redirects to an unrelated third-party site — dead source on the Season 2 program file
summary: registry/programs/polygon-community-grants-season-2.yaml cites https://polygon.technology/grow as a source. That path now 301-redirects to https://hadronfc.com/, an unrelated business with no evident connection to Polygon — looks like an expired/squatted path rather than a legitimate migration target, so it should not be treated as a 'dead website -> live redirect' fact-lane fix. Separately, polygon.technology's current homepage and nav no longer surface any dedicated grants/funding page at all (only docs, resources, and an early-access contact form), which may mean the Community Grants Program has gone fully dormant since Season 2 concluded rather than continuing under a new season. Recommend the owner verify whether a Season 3 exists anywhere (e.g. Polygon forum/Questbook) and, if not, drop the dead /grow citation and consider whether polygon's org-level funding.apply_url (questbook) is still current.

summary: shuttleworthfoundation.org/funding/fellowship-programme states two annual intakes (March 1 start, applications close November 1; September 1 start, applications close May 1) as if live. title: Source cited for ASF's Responsible AI / Tooling Initiative claims (apache.org/foundation/grants.html) now 404s
summary: The org profile describes a March 2025 Tooling Initiative and an April 2026 $10M Responsible AI Initiative (seeded with $1.75M from Anthropic and Alpha-Omega), sourced from apache.org/foundation/grants.html. That URL now returns 404. The parent page (apache.org/foundation/) and the governance page (how-it-works.html) that were checked this round describe ASF's structure and sponsorship model but do not restate the initiative details, so this pass could not reverify or refresh those specific funding-program claims. Recommend the owner locate a current source (ASF blog/news) for the Responsible AI and Tooling Initiatives before the next audit, or soften the profile if the page is confirmed gone rather than moved.
